title: Laredo's District IV Bulky Waste Collection Is Today: What to Put Out, and What to Leave
excerpt: The City of Laredo collects bulky waste in District IV today, October 27, 2026 — furniture, mattresses, bicycles and appliances, with strict placement rules and fees for extra items.
content:
Today is bulky waste day for Laredo's District IV. City crews will collect large household items that regular trash service cannot handle — furniture, mattresses, bicycles and appliances — from residential accounts in the district. KGNS reported the collection on October 26, and the city's schedule lists October 27 as the District IV date.

The rules matter, because crews will not take everything, and they will not come onto private property. Residents may set out up to four items at no cost. Extra items carry fees: $15 for the first additional item, $10 for the second, and $5 for each item after that. Items must be placed at least 10 feet away from large objects such as cars or fences, and out by 6 a.m.

Eligible items include mattresses, bicycles and furniture. Excluded items include electronic waste, batteries, car parts and hazardous liquids — those need other disposal routes and will be left behind. Residents who need to dispose of more than four items can contact 3-1-1 to schedule a special pickup.

Why the city runs it district by district

Bulky waste is the kind of trash that becomes a neighborhood problem when there is no outlet for it: a broken sofa on a side yard, a mattress leaning against a fence, an old appliance behind a garage. Left long enough, it draws illegal dumping, pests and code complaints. A scheduled, district-by-district collection gives residents a legal, free-or-cheap way to clear it — and gives crews a route they can actually finish.

The trade-off is that the schedule only helps residents who know about it and get items out on time. District IV residents who miss today wait for the next cycle, while the rest of the city's schedule continues: District V on November 12, District VI on November 19, and District VII on December 4.

Questions worth asking

How many District IV households use the service, and how much bulky material does a single collection day divert from alleys and vacant lots? The city publishes the schedule; it does not publish collection totals in the same place. Residents who want the excluded items — electronics, batteries, hazardous liquids — picked up should ask what drop-off options exist, because a resident told “no” at the curb without an alternative is a resident more likely to dump illegally.

For today, the practical message is simple: four items, curbside, 10 feet clear, by 6 a.m.
